newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Komag says Q3 output fell 23 pct.
newsitem.headline: Komag says Q3 output fell 23 pct.

text.p: U.S.-based Komag Inc says output at its U.S. and Malaysian factories fell 23 percent quarter-on quarter in the third quarter of 1996, Malaysia's national news agency Bernama said on Friday.
Komag is the world's largest supplier of thin-film media for computer hard disk drives.

Komag produced 10.7 million units in the third quarter of 1996 to September 29, compared to 13.9 million units in the second quarter of the year. The second quarter production figure was a record for the company.
The Bernama report did not differentiate between U.S. and Malaysian production figures.
"Low start-up yields on new products and several additional non-recurring events contributed to the third quarter's output reduction," a company source told Bernama.
Electronic and electrical products made in Malaysia account for roughly half the country's exports.

Komag employs around 1,400 workers in its plant in Penang, northern Malaysia, which has become the country's "Silicon Valley" over the past two decades. The company also has a plant in the eastern state of Sarawak on Borneo island, which employs a few hundred people.
The announcements came on the release in the United States of Komag's third-quarter 1996 financial results. Net sales were $131.5 million, down from $132.8 million in the third quarter of 1995.
